activity_context.topic_title: Differentiating Curves Given in Polar Form

feedback.problem:
Find the slope $m$ of the tangent line to the polar curve $r=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )$ at $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{8}$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\theta ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ), \\ {x}^{′}(\theta ) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Do not round the answer.

$m=$ 
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ we use the rule

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )}.
$$

We have,

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{8}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{8}) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Hence, the slope $m$ of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =3\pi /8} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{8})}{{x}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{8})} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}{(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
